title: The symmetric algebra commutes with base change
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $M$ an $R$-module, with symmetric algebras $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$, $\iota_M:M\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ and $\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_RM)$, $\iota_{S\otimes M}$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. Let $\beta:\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_RM)$ be the $R$-algebra homomorphism with $\beta(\iota_M(m))=\iota_{S\otimes M}(1\otimes m)$. Then the $S$-algebra homomorphism $S\otimes_R\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}_S(S\otimes_RM)$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s\,\beta(a)$, is an isomorphism. (For $S=R_f$ the localization at the powers of $f\in R$: $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)_f\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{R_f}(M_f)$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0C6F (lemma-tensor-algebra-localization, line 2386: S^{-1}T_R(M) = T_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M), similarly for Sym; proof omitted, hint: Lemma 00DE tensor-product-localization) is the localization case; the general base change follows from the universal properties: for a commutative S-algebra B, Hom_{S-alg}(S⊗_R Sym_R M, B) = Hom_{R-alg}(Sym_R M, B) = Hom_R(M, B) = Hom_S(S⊗_R M, B) = Hom_{S-alg}(Sym_S(S⊗_R M), B), compatibly with the map of the statement
